texts: mixed: all the content is captured, but 'between A and B' has no supported two-landmark position form, so the parse had to improvise a three-place link that no reasoning rule reaches and that a later re-parse may render differently. If you want the position to be stable and queryable, split it into two ordinary position statements: 'The harbor lies on one side of the village square, and the Watch lies on the other side.'

mixed: the parse is faithful, but 'weekly' sitting inside the noun phrase lands only as a plain property of the market, so nothing records the recurrence and 'how often does the market run?' finds nothing. Move the frequency out of the noun phrase into the clause: 'A market runs in the village square every week.'

bad: the four goods are stacked onto one delivery event, which reads as a single joint shipment of all four rather than four things the boats bring, and there is no supported way to split a coordinated object list inside a generic rule of this shape; 'down' was also dropped, widening the origin to the coast at large. Give each commodity its own finite clause: 'Boats from down the coast bring grain to the market. Boats from down the coast bring salt to the market. Boats from down the coast bring cloth to the market. Boats from down the coast bring ironmongery to the market.' If 'down' is not load-bearing, plain 'from the coast' also avoids a residual problem — nothing records what the direction is measured from.

good. the definite plural yields both a group-level use event and a per-villager rule, 'the market salt' keeps its link to salt, and 'for cooking' is recorded as the purpose without claiming any particular cooking happened.
good. 'imported' correctly restricts the claim to imported salt rather than salt at large, and the denial lands as a rule at strength zero.

bad: 'Mire-essence distillation' is a kind, not a thing that can be the doer of one particular event, so the parse produced a single flat requiring event with a kind in the actor slot — a shape that fires nothing and that additionally asserts one specific quantity of sea-water from the local pools exists. Make the generality explicit so it becomes a rule any distillation can trigger: 'Every mire-essence distillation requires sea-water from the local pools.' One limitation remains either way: 'requires' is still read as though the required sea-water exists.
